skill.name: service-mesh-observability
skill.description: Design metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerts for Istio, Linkerd, and OpenTelemetry service mesh deployments.

skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, standard in-cluster addresses, listener bindings, and a PromQL regex. Semantic review found insecure Kiali access defaults and disabled TLS for the Jaeger exporter in example configurations.

remediation.issue: The Kiali example enables anonymous authentication and grants visibility across every namespace.
remediation.suggestion: Use token or OpenID authentication, restrict accessible namespaces, and enforce least-privilege Kubernetes RBAC.

remediation.issue: The OpenTelemetry Jaeger exporter disables TLS.
remediation.suggestion: Enable TLS, validate the Jaeger collector certificate, and document any development-only exception.

semantic_findings.title: Kiali Example Enables Broad Anonymous Access
semantic_findings.description: The Kiali template selects anonymous authentication and the wildcard namespace scope. A reachable deployment could expose mesh topology and telemetry across all namespaces.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly sets the authentication strategy to anonymous and accessible_namespaces to a wildcard. Both settings are visible in the cited YAML.

semantic_findings.title: Jaeger Exporter Disables TLS
semantic_findings.description: The OpenTelemetry example sets insecure transport for the Jaeger exporter. Telemetry may cross the cluster without encryption or collector identity verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exporter configuration explicitly sets tls.insecure to true for the Jaeger endpoint. This disables secure transport in the provided deployment template.

content.value_statement: Service mesh telemetry can be difficult to configure, correlate, and operate. This skill provides practical patterns for metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerts.
actual_capabilities: Explains metrics, traces, logs, and golden signals for service meshes.
Provides PromQL patterns for request rate, errors, latency, connections, and request size.
Outlines Istio integration with Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, and OpenTelemetry.
Shows Linkerd Viz commands for routes, live traffic, service edges, and dashboards.
Provides sample dashboards and alerts for errors, latency, topology, and certificate expiration.
limitations: The examples require adaptation for each cluster, mesh version, namespace layout, and security policy.
The skill does not deploy resources, inspect a live cluster, or verify generated configurations.
Several templates are simplified and omit production controls such as authentication, TLS, storage, and network policies.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the audited file structure.

use_cases.title: Plan a Mesh Monitoring Baseline
use_cases.description: Define golden signals, dashboards, alerts, and trace sampling before a new mesh enters production.

use_cases.title: Investigate Service Latency
use_cases.description: Combine service metrics, dependency views, and distributed traces to isolate slow upstream or downstream calls.

use_cases.title: Standardize Telemetry Across Teams
use_cases.description: Create shared Prometheus queries, Grafana panels, and OpenTelemetry conventions for multiple application teams.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Observability Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the essential metrics, traces, and logs for my [Istio or Linkerd] mesh. Include the golden signals and simple validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear monitoring baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Service Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dashboard for [service name] using [mesh] metrics. Include request rate, error rate, P99 latency, saturation, and useful filters.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a focused operational dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Mesh Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an investigation plan for [symptom] in [mesh]. Correlate Prometheus metrics, traces, topology, and proxy logs. Include verification checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operator needs a structured incident workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Production Telemetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Design production observability for [cluster details]. Cover OpenTelemetry pipelines, sampling, cardinality, retention, authentication, TLS, RBAC, alerts, and rollout validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect needs an environment-specific production design.

output_examples.input: Define a baseline dashboard for an Istio checkout service.
output: Overview: request volume, success rate, P50 latency, P99 latency, and active connections.
Breakdowns: source workload, destination service, response code, route, and cluster.
Alerts: sustained error rate, latency threshold, traffic anomaly, and certificate expiration.

output_examples.input: Help investigate high latency between frontend and payments.
output: Confirm the latency increase by destination and compare P50 with P99.
Inspect service topology for unexpected routes, retries, or dependency changes.
Use correlated traces to identify the slow span and validate the affected workload.

output_examples.input: Recommend trace sampling for development and production.
output_examples.output: Use complete sampling in small development environments when affordable. Start production sampling near one to ten percent, then adjust using volume and cost.

best_practices: Validate metric names, labels, ports, and APIs against the deployed mesh version.
Use representative traffic and failure tests to verify dashboards, traces, and alerts before production rollout.
Protect observability endpoints with authentication, TLS, RBAC, namespace restrictions, and network policies.
anti_patterns: Do not apply example manifests without reviewing security, capacity, and compatibility requirements.
Do not use high-cardinality labels or complete production trace sampling without cost controls.
Do not expose dashboards, collectors, or telemetry backends through anonymous or unrestricted access.

faq.question: Which service meshes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Istio and Linkerd, with related patterns for Kiali, Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry.

faq.question: Can it generate Prometheus queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides patterns for traffic, errors, latency, TCP connections, and request size.

faq.question: Does it deploy monitoring components?
faq.answer: No. It supplies guidance and examples, but an operator must review, apply, and validate every change.

faq.question: Are the configurations production ready?
faq.answer: No. They require version checks and stronger controls for authentication, TLS, RBAC, storage, networking, and capacity.

faq.question: Can it help troubleshoot incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure investigations using metrics, traces, topology, and logs when you provide the environment and symptoms.

faq.question: How should trace sampling be selected?
faq.answer: Choose sampling from traffic volume, diagnostic needs, retention, and cost. Validate the rate under representative workloads.
